column3: SQL trace flag off or sql-trace panel off gives SqlCapture DISABLED, as BootUI's recorder.isEnabled() = sqlTrace.isEnabled() && isPanelEnabled(SQL_TRACE) (BootUiAutoConfiguration.java:803; SqlCapture.java:60-66, v2.3.0): a check that needs SQL is UNAVAILABLE with the DISABLED reason, an optional read gets the caveat.

DEFAULT TAKEN, owner may reverse: with the flag on and the panel off, the DISABLED text names the sql-trace panel, not SHARPIT_SQL_TRACE_ENABLED=false (BootUI's one text names its flag for both causes, which blames the wrong switch).

Ported from SqlCapture.java:60-66 and SqlTraceRecorder.hasWrappedDataSource (v2.3.0:530-553), with sharpit's recorders in the text (SQLAlchemy 2.0+ and the sqlite3 module). The fact is per context and costs nothing per statement: a SQLAlchemy engine that was ever in the context's registry (EngineRegistry.seen_any, write-once because engines are held weakly; known when the engine connects, as BootUI's registerDataSource runs at wrap time; with no database panel enabled the registry is not fed, so attaching the SQL listeners stands for it), or, with no database panel enabled (the registry is then not fed and the engines are unknown), the attach of the SQL listeners (CaptureState.engines_unseen: DEFAULT TAKEN, owner may reverse; true for any process that imported SQLAlchemy 2.x there), or, for raw sqlite3 (no wrap-time object), a write-once flag set on the first sqlite3 statement delivered to the context (CaptureState.sqlite_delivered). R2DBC has no analogue.
DEFAULT TAKEN, owner may reverse (sharpit-only state, BootUI has no detachable hooks): one SQL hook detached from a source in use is recorded-except naming it; every one detached is not recorded.

DEFAULT TAKEN, owner may reverse: RuntimeInsightsService.java:1014 drops the unseen caveats when a check is PARTIAL; sharpit keeps the SQL-capture caveat there, so a partial check over half-recorded SQL does not read as complete.

Ported: the SQL Trace panel, its insights and the MCP/CLI reads are unavailable while no database is in use (BootUI SqlTraceControllerSupport.report:65 and SqlTraceInsightsService.insights:62 answer unavailable while no DataSource is wrapped). Deviation, DEFAULT TAKEN, owner may reverse: one text (the not-recorded text) replaces BootUI's two ("No DataSource bean is available" / "No DataSource has been wrapped for tracing yet."), and raw sqlite3 has no wrap-time object, so an idle raw-sqlite3 app reads unavailable until its first statement (the panel and the insights agree). A suspended hook is a capture state, not an absent database: the panel stays available and says it is not capturing.

sqlastats keeps its own availability (flag off, or SQLAlchemy 2.0+ not imported): BootUI's Hibernate statistics follow the SessionFactory, never the SQL recorder (HibernateStatisticsService.report:38-47, v2.3.0), so no engine attached is not a reason for it.
